question: In which of the following network topologies do the connected components make a closed loop?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ring topology**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ring network topology**

 
 
• The **physical and logical configuration **of a network's nodes and links is known as its **network topology**.
 
• Devices like **switches, routers, and software** with switch and router functionality are typically included in nodes.
 
• A **graph** is a common way to represent network topologies.
 
• When two computers are joined to **create a ring**, the topology is known as a **ring topology**.
 
• The nodes are linked together in a **closed-loop manner** in the ring network topology. T
 
• The message passing is **circular and unidirectional**.
 
• **Dual Ring Topology **is another way to make it bidirectional by adding two connections between each Network Node.
 
• This topology primarily utilises a **token-based system**, and each token moves in a single direction in a loop.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If a token is available in a ring topology, **the node can take it, attach the data, and the destination address, and then leave the token for communication**.
 
• The data is taken out by the receiver when this token reaches the destination node, freeing it up to carry the subsequent data.
 
• The most common type of ring network is a **metro network**, which is based on Synchronous Optical Network technology.
 
• Network topologies explain how **networks are set up and where traffic flows are located in relation to one another**.
 
• The** diagrams **can be used by administrators t**o decide where each node should be located and the best path for traffic flow**.
